name: Curitiba
title: Curitiba Urban Planning, Oscar Niemeyer Museum & Paraná Culture Heritage Host
worldview: An empire is a grid of copper, transit buses, and green parks. We designed our city in the high, dry Paraná plateau as a 'garden city' with wide English parks and the glass eye of the Niemeyer museum, proving that modern technology thrives best where there is a relaxed, open climate of universities and bus-side social circles. We code the future.

learning_objectives: Understand the pioneering urban planning of Curitiba under Mayor Jaime Lerner in the 1970s, focusing on the Bus-Rapid Transit (BRT) system.
Analyze the design of the Oscar Niemeyer Museum (Novo Museu), evaluating how its sculptural, 'Eye'-shaped concrete tower projects modern art.
Evaluate how the implementation of pedestrian zones (Rua das Flores) and public green parks solved urban flooding and transportation crises.
discussion_prompts: How did a regional, high-density city on the southern plateau of Brazil (Curitiba) manage to become the world capital of sustainable urban transit, inventing the BRT system that has been copied by cities globally?
Why did the architect Oscar Niemeyer choose to build a colossal, eye-shaped concrete tower (the 'Eye' Museum) to display contemporary art, and how does this challenge classical geometry?
Can a historic, highly planned city preserve its green, water-rich environment (which relied on integrating parks into floodbasins) under the pressure of rapid concrete real estate growth?
